Subject: Questions on DR approach and evidence for RFP — RTO/RPO expectations

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the DR capability package you sent with the RFP response. A couple of clarifications from our risk team before we lock the acceptance criteria in the SOW:

- RTO / RPO: We need a firm statement for the SLA you can commit to under the Dedicated and Private deployment options. CityLight requires RPO <= 60s for core routing/transaction state and an RTO (full service recovery) target of <= 30 minutes for critical traffic. Can you confirm what you will commit to, by deployment mode?

- Failover mode and data consistency: For cross-region failover, do you operate warm-standby (async replication + catch-up) or synchronous replication? What happens to in-flight requests and cached KV state?

- Automation & triggers: Do you provide automatic detection and automated failover, or is the cutover manual with runbook steps? What are the pre- and post-cutover checks?

- Evidence: Please attach the playbook extract you use for customer DR rehearsals, recent test logs (redacted), and any runbook sections that cover DNS/traffic cutover, database replay, and rollback. We also want a proposed window to run a joint simulation.

Appreciate a short mutual-action plan and a list of the artifacts you will produce for our auditors.

Paul

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on DR approach and evidence for RFP — RTO/RPO expectations

Paul — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise response and a proposed MAP (mutual action plan). I've attached the runbook extract and a condensed evidence pack.

Summary commitments (by deployment mode):
- Hosted (shared): RPO: best-effort, typically < 120s for session metadata; RTO: failover detection + routing fallback within 30 minutes operational target. Not SLA-backed for shared tier in the standard plan — we recommend Dedicated for contractual commitments.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): RPO: <= 60s for persisted transaction state (typical configuration: async replication + write-ahead logs streamed cross-region); RTO: <= 30 minutes for service restoration to routed traffic (target in SLO; available for inclusion in contract terms).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): RPO: configurable down to <= 1s with synchronous replication profiles for ultra-critical workloads (depends on customer network latency); RTO: contractual target of <= 30 minutes for full traffic cutover if configured with warm-standby or active-active for <10min.

Technical approach (short):
- Data replication: Primary strategy is continuous WAL/append-stream replication to secondary region + periodic KV checkpointing. For Dedicated we operate a staged async replication pipeline with near-real-time replay; for Private customers we can enable sync replication if the network/private link supports it.
- Cache/KV handling: During failover we rebuild runtime caches from persisted checkpoints and from the streamed WAL. In-flight requests that have not been acknowledged to persistent storage are treated as non-committed — we mark a bounded window as "at-risk" and expose that in the post-failover report. We provide sequences to drain/in-flight-handling in the runbook.
- Automation & triggers: Detection is hybrid: automated health checks + orchestration policy. Default is automated detection (node-level and region-level health signals) that notifies on-call and initiates a staged failover pipeline. Final cutover (traffic DNS/edge re-route) is typically manual for production-critical customers unless explicit automatic cutover is agreed in the contract. Manual cutover is designed to be repeatable within the RTO target.

Operational guarantees and test evidence we will provide:
- Redacted simulation logs from the last three rehearsals (control-plane events, timestamps)
- Playbook extract that shows pre-cutover checks, failover steps, post-cutover validation checklist (attached: redwood-dr-runbook-v1.pdf and dr-runbook-extract.txt)
- A sample post-test evidence bundle (screenshots, edge routing snapshots, and timestamped event list)

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) CityLight to confirm acceptance criteria (RTO<=30m, RPO<=60s for critical streams) — by 2026-09-03.
2) Redwood to provide secured evidence bundle and a condensed runbook — by 2026-09-06 (attached).
3) Joint simulation planning call — propose 2026-09-15 02:00 UTC for a non-production rehearsal. Redwood will host the session and provide a day-of runbook and contact list.
4) Simulation execution and evidence handoff — 2026-09-15 (window).
5) After-action review and any remediation commitments — within 5 business days of the simulation.

Attachments included: redwood-dr-runbook-v1.pdf (playbook extract), dr-runbook-extract.txt (cutover checklists). Also sharing a calendar invite ICS for the proposed simulation separately.

If CityLight can confirm the acceptance criteria and the window, we will lock the simulation and prepare the on-day runbook and billing/traffic expectations.

-Jonas

Subject: Re: Questions on DR approach and evidence for RFP — RTO/RPO expectations

Jonas — thanks for the detailed breakdown and the runbook extract. A couple of follow-ups before we sign off:

1) We can accept the Dedicated commitments you listed (RPO <= 60s / RTO <= 30m) if you can confirm the post-cutover validation steps will show no data divergence for the last acknowledged sequence ID and that the at-risk window will be scoped and reported.

2) For the Private deployment, CityLight will require the synchronous replication profile for core transaction streams. Please confirm network bandwidth/latency pre-reqs for that profile and whether Redwood will support the network validation.

3) During the simulation we need to understand billing behaviour for token consumption and whether test traffic will be billed normally or under a test policy. Also need the day-of escalation contacts and a primary phone line.

If you can confirm those three items we will confirm the MAP and sign the testing waiver.

Paul
